failures.criterion: Architect acceptance item 7: the file set against main and every lane ci-ok. The required ci-filters gate must be green at the head.
failures.evidence: ci-filters is settled FAILURE at head f7d47578 (run 41352059014, job 124984937998, https://github.com/sjawhar/legion/actions/runs/41352059014/job/124984937998): '55 CI filter problem(s)', e.g. 'dispatch reads packages/envoy/internal/kvwatch/scan.go, which its filter dispatch does not match, so a change to it skips the job'. Root cause introduced by this PR: internal/dispatch/redeliver/sweep.go now imports internal/kvwatch (DrainExistingKeys); base 0642a37a's sweep.go has no such import (verified with git show 0642a37a:.../sweep.go). cmd/dispatch depends on redeliver, so the dispatch, dispatch_browser_multiprocess, dispatch_memory and dispatch_multiprocess jobs now read packages/envoy/internal/kvwatch/* via `go list -deps ./cmd/dispatch`, but those four path filters in .github/workflows/ci.yaml (the `dispatch` filter is lines ~235-273) do not list packages/envoy/internal/kvwatch/*. Fix: add `- 'packages/envoy/internal/kvwatch/*'` to each of those four filters so a change to kvwatch no longer skips the dispatch jobs. The check's own red run is the regression lock; no Go test applies. envoy-go-race (the behavioural race lane over redeliver/architecture/kvwatch) passed at this head.

proof.criterion: 2i: the running sweep reads only the deliveries the index says are due, and a failed delivery whose attempts have left the listing window is still redelivered when due (never lost over time).
proof.surface: A booted envoy-dispatch (head) against a real nats-server v2.10.29 and a fake GitHub whose attempt listing is empty, so every redelivery request it receives came from the sweep's own index. Bucket seeded with a due-indexed record, a due-unindexed record (no entry, no marker), a later-indexed record due 90 s on, a lost-entry record whose Pending names a key never written, and 2,000 not-due noise records (e4seed/e4.sh).
proof.observed: Sweep 1 (deliveries=2 index_entries=2) redelivered due-indexed (1001) and the back-filled due-unindexed (1002); sweep 2 two minutes later (deliveries=1 index_entries=1) redelivered later-indexed (1003) as soon as it came due. Final bucket check: entries moved forward, no strays, 2,000 noise records never read. Nothing lost across sweeps.
proof.negativeControl: lost-entry (1005), whose index entry was never written, was never requested by the head build (requests 1001,1002,1003 only). The same bucket on base (bash e4.sh base) requested 1001,1002,1005 in one sweep reading all 2,004 records, so the index selection is what the head build relies on.
